# MCP capabilities

This guide inventories the production direct-tool registry compiled into this build. Family, focused membership, and recovery visibility are internal discovery metadata, not authorization grants or client-visible MCP recommendation fields.

## Discovery contract

The normal executor surface derives its catalogue from executable operation contracts and does not read the profiles or overlays below. Its discovery surface is currently not user-configurable.

On the legacy direct-tool transport, the default `complete` profile advertises every production-registry tool. The opt-in `focused` profile advertises only the rows marked focused below and is intentionally lossy. Stored family and per-tool overlays remain an internal compatibility and emergency-rollback seam, not a supported user-facing setting. `bootstrap` and `read_guide` are recovery tools and remain shown after every legacy overlay.

Legacy exposure controls affect discovery only: omission from `tools/list` can make a tool undiscoverable and can break workflows that refer to it. A hidden tool remains callable by exact name when the caller already knows it, but the filter does not grant a capability or bypass ordinary authorization and validation. Custom overlays are not dependency-solved.

## Interpretation read opt-in

`get_record`, record-producing `query_record`, and `render_record` accept direct-call `include_interpretation:true`. It defaults false; absent and explicit false preserve the established payload and perform no attribution/provenance work. The opt-in is live-only and caller-authorized in one snapshot. It is limited to 50 returned bearers, 100 claims, 32 evidence rows per claim, and 256 total evidence rows, distinct inspections, and inspection-output records. Request-wide overflow returns an unavailable projection with no claim/evidence identifiers or per-bearer/global cardinality; delegation, confidence, and counts never establish endorsement, truth, or consensus. Raw claims and claim-specific Why remain exclusive to `read_attributions`.

The direct query flag is not part of saved-query v0.2 and rejects non-record terminals, `as_of`, and federated query fan-out. Federated exact get may forward it within the same 50-bearer cap; unsupported sources fail explicitly. Postgres-server and Turso-local reject the opt-in until they implement the qualified projection rather than silently omitting it. `query_sql` remains attribution-blind.

Exact compact UTF-8 `result.tools` descriptor arrays:

- `focused`: 27 tools, 71836 bytes
- `complete`: 82 tools, 209910 bytes
